[DB-1] Checkout: coupon + order writes not atomic, N+1 item ops
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L260)
Evidence: coupon quantity is read and prisma.coupon.update is executed outside any transaction before order creation; the existing-order branch updates/creates/deletes orderItems with sequential await calls inside for...of loops (many separate txns). This allows races (coupon overspend/duplicate users) and issues partial commits while issuing N+1 DB queries per item.  
Impact: breaks correctness and throughput during spikes — concurrent checkouts (≈200–500 simultaneous) will cause oversold coupons, duplicate/partial orders and large bursts of DB queries that overload the DB.  
Fix: wrap coupon decrement, user create/upsert and full order+orderItems upsert/delete in a single prisma.$transaction (or use conditional UPDATE/RETURNING and bulk upserts) and batch item writes instead of per-item queries.

finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Checkout: coupon + order writes not atomic, N+1 item ops
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L260)
Evidence: coupon quantity is read and prisma.coupon.update is executed outside any transaction before order creation; the existing-order branch updates/creates/deletes orderItems with sequential await calls inside for...of loops (many separate txns). This allows races (coupon overspend/duplicate users) and issues partial commits while issuing N+1 DB queries per item.  
Impact: breaks correctness and throughput during spikes — concurrent checkouts (≈200–500 simultaneous) will cause oversold coupons, duplicate/partial orders and large bursts of DB queries that overload the DB.  
Fix: wrap coupon decrement, user create/upsert and full order+orderItems upsert/delete in a single prisma.$transaction (or use conditional UPDATE/RETURNING and bulk upserts) and batch item writes instead of per-item queries.

[DB-2] Missing indexes on orders and order_items used in checkout
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L1200)
Evidence: code frequently queries orders by cartId/status and order_items by orderId (e.g., order.findFirst({ where: { cartId, status: ... } }), orderItem.findMany({ where: { orderId } })), but the schema has no @@index for order.cartId, order.status, or OrderItem.orderId/productId.  
Impact: causes full-table scans as tables grow; critical checkout paths will degrade or timeout once orders/order_items reach hundreds of thousands — expect failures around a few hundred to a few thousand concurrent checkouts depending on table size and DB CPU.  
Fix: add targeted indexes such as @@index([cartId, status]) on Order and @@index([orderId]) on OrderItem (and consider composite indexes for frequent filters/sorts).

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-4] Unbounded product listing (no pagination)
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (L1-L160)
Evidence: products are returned via prisma.product.findMany({ include: { colors: ... }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' } }) with no take/skip or cursor pagination.  
Impact: returning all products and their colors will create large queries and payloads as the catalog grows (noticeable at 10k+ products, severe at 100k+), increasing response latency and bandwidth costs.  
Fix: add cursor or page-based pagination (take/skip or cursor-based) and limit eager-loaded relations (or paginate/includes by demand).

[DB-5] Serverless DB pool risk (singleton present, no pooler)
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: Prisma client is memoized on globalThis (good), but no evidence of a connection pooler/Data Proxy in config/DATABASE_URL or environment.  
Impact: while the singleton reduces connections per lambda instance, many cold starts + high concurrency can still produce hundreds of DB connections and exhaust DB limits (problematic above ~500 concurrent connections).  
Fix: front Prisma with a pooler (pgbouncer) or use Prisma Data Proxy / managed pooling and tune DATABASE_URL/pool settings.

--- INFO ---

[DB-6] Prisma client memoized for dev to reduce connections
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: globalForPrisma.prisma caches the PrismaClient in non-production to reuse the client across module reloads.
